newsitem.title: UK: Turkish missile exploded under British airliner.
newsitem.headline: Turkish missile exploded under British airliner.

text.p: British Airways said on Friday that a missile exploded some 10,000 feet (3,000 metres) below one of its airliners flying over Turkey after staff failed to feed details of a planned military exercise into a computer.
"It was a mistake in that the information should have been entered into the system," a spokesman said.
No one was hurt in the incident last June aboard a flight from Islamabad, Pakistan, to Manchester, northern England, as the missile went off about five miles (eight km) away from the Boeing 747 jet.
"At no time was there are any threat whatsoever to the safety or aircraft or its passengers," he said.
The spokesman said airline chiefs had ordered staff in its Navigation Services and Flight Crew Briefing departments to change the way they work.
"Procedures have already been reinforced to ensure that changes to flight information are immediately put into the flight navigation system," he said.
"This was very much an isolated incident. It has never happened before," he added.
London's Evening Standard newspaper reported that the airliner had been routed along Turkish airway UA17, which passes just north of Istanbul on June 4.
Some 11 days earlier Istanbul Air Traffic Control had informed world airlines that the airway would be closed from June 1 and June 8 because of military activity.

Such information is normally routinely fed into the computer which produces British Airways flight plans. But the spokesman said in this case the two departments involved apparently left this task to each other.
